sampling_model.design: An i.i.d. randomized experiment with fixed finite stratum set \(\mathcal J\), fixed finite action set \(\mathcal A\), and known action probabilities \(e_{ja}\).
sampling_model.units: For each local row \(n\), the full units \(O_{n1},\ldots,O_{nn}\) are i.i.d. from \(P_n\), while the planner observes only \(O^{\mathrm{obs}}_{ni}=(X_{ni},A_{ni},Y_{ni})\) and hence only \(\mathcal F_n^{\mathrm{obs}}\).
sampling_model.treatment: Conditional randomization satisfies \(Y^{\mathrm{pot}}\perp A\mid X\), consistency, and \(e_{ja}\ge e_{\min}\).
sampling_model.overlap: Every stratum has \(p_j\ge p_{\min}\), every randomized action has \(e_{ja}\ge e_{\min}\), and every benchmark action has \(b_{ja}\ge\beta\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Finite randomized cells are estimated by within-cell Hájek means and stratum masses by empirical frequencies. These observed estimators generate \(\widehat{\mathfrak F}_n\), the only frontier supplied to the temperature selector. The Gaussian approximation envelope for the distinct oracle regret path is derived from bounded outcomes, cell mass, and overlap in \(\mathrm{lem:cell\mbox{-}gaussian}\), rather than assumed for the estimator.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: For fixed positive \(\lambda\), \(nR_\lambda(\widehat\theta)\) converges to one-half of a Gaussian quadratic form.
A predetermined diverging inverse temperature yields root-\(n\) asymptotic linearity for the unsmoothed optimal-policy value.
Convergent binary treatment rules are represented by rules in a shifted Gaussian limit experiment.
A scalar empirical-process supremum is coupled nonasymptotically to the corresponding Gaussian supremum.
The concentration function of a standardized Gaussian-process supremum is bounded by its expected supremum.
Ordinary bootstrap consistency under a Gaussian limit is equivalent to full differentiability of the transformation.
Gaussian-vector maxima admit covariance comparison and anti-concentration bounds under arbitrary correlation.
A separation-of-variables transformation reduces Gaussian rectangle probabilities to bounded multiple integration.
Taylor expansion, interval analysis, and automatic differentiation self-validate Gaussian rectangle probabilities.
Recursive integration evaluates noncentered Gaussian orthant probabilities for positive-definite correlation matrices.
Joint Gaussian critical values give coverage after selecting a series dimension from the searched specification set.

body.tldr: A finite-stratum randomized lottery generates a continuum of benchmark-centered Gibbs rules indexed by a KL penalty. The normalized oracle-minus-estimated regret is compactified into one continuous path whose hard endpoint uses benchmark weights on every maximizing set and whose high-penalty endpoint is a projected categorical-covariance quadratic form. The main result is a quantitative uniform Gaussian approximation for this entire nonlinear path. An observed plug-in welfare frontier, computed only from cell estimates and empirical stratum weights, supplies the operational temperature selector, while a deterministic simultaneous-event bridge transfers coverage to the oracle regret at that selected temperature. An effective interval-and-Gaussian-integration algorithm takes rational data or named interval oracles, emits a machine-checkable directed-rounding certificate within an explicit work bound, and falls back to a finite analytic Gaussian-tail certificate when adaptive integration does not close. The resulting atom-safe envelope is valid after every observed-data-measurable temperature choice. Sharp anti-concentration of the nonlinear Gaussian supremum remains an explicit open question rather than an assumption.

project_justification.gap: Fixed positive KL penalties have a quadratic regret law, while the hard assignment boundary and softmax inference for one predetermined smoothing sequence are studied separately. No published result gives a quantitative joint law or a certified critical value over the full penalty menu.
project_justification.niche: Finite multiaction lotteries create a tractable but nonstandard function-valued statistic: its interior coordinates are nonlinear Gaussian transforms, its hard endpoint is directionally differentiable with benchmark-weighted multiway ties, and its opposite endpoint has a different quadratic normalization.
project_justification.fill: The project derives the primitive finite-cell Gaussian certificate, matches both endpoints, proves an explicit tie-slab coupling rate in \(C([0,1])\), defines a sample-computable plug-in frontier and its observed-data sigma-field, and turns a one-sided lower CDF bracket with effective input names, directed rounding, a checkable output witness, and a finite fallback bound into computably honest inference after an operational frontier-based temperature choice without assuming away atoms.

body.related_work: Fang--Ridder--Xie studies benchmark-centered KL assignment and proves a quadratic regret limit for each fixed positive penalty; its Conclusion leaves data-driven penalty choice open, and its deterministic binary analysis is separate. The finite-cell dummy-feature inclusion in that framework and the equality of the \(t=1\) quadratic formula with its fixed-penalty specialization are used only as sanity and reduction checks, not as contributions or claimed extensions. Its three-arm commitment-savings frontier motivates an illustration, but no finite-stratification adequacy claim is made. Whitehouse--Chen--Austern--Syrgkanis uses softmax smoothing to estimate one unsmoothed optimal-policy value along a predetermined diverging temperature and permits exact ties, but its uniform tie weights and scalar target differ from the benchmark-weighted regret path. Hirano--Porter supplies the shifted-Gaussian local decision experiment for binary hard treatment choice, not a multiaction path law. Chernozhukov--Chetverikov--Kato supplies finite-net Gaussian coupling and anti-concentration for suprema of Gaussian processes; those results inform the proof, but \(G(h,Z_V)\) is nonlinear in \(Z_V\) and is not itself a Gaussian process. Fang--Santos identifies the directional derivative and bootstrap issue at max-type boundaries, while its quantile conclusions do not provide certified atom-safe continuum calibration here. Genz, Wang--Kennedy, and Miwa--Hayter--Kuriki provide Gaussian rectangle or orthant integration components; their algorithms do not reduce or certify the proposed nonlinear continuum sublevel event. Kang supplies the logic that a simultaneous band survives a tuning choice computed from an observed linear series path; it does not distinguish a sample-computable selection frontier from an unobserved oracle regret target or cover the changing endpoint geometry and numerical certification here.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The one-sided algorithm terminates and certifies coverage because the work-capped refinement has an analytic Gaussian-tail fallback, but it need not return a critical value within a prescribed numerical distance of \(Q_{1-\alpha}^{\mathrm{LF}}\). Without the open concentration modulus or exact enumeration of every flat stratum, ambiguous boundary boxes can encode an atom and prevent a two-sided value-width certificate. The rational fallback \(2B_\gamma^++(B_\gamma^+)^2/2\) can be conservative.
body.honest_scope: The theorem is uniform only for fixed \(J\) and \(K\), positive benchmark probabilities, positive stratum and treatment probabilities, bounded outcomes, compact local contrasts, and a covariance spectrum bounded away from zero. It excludes boundary benchmarks, singular covariance, growing action or stratum counts, disappearing cells, and continuous covariates without a prespecified finite stratification. The finite-cell embedding in Fang--Ridder--Xie and the \(t=1\) fixed-penalty quadratic equality are sanity and reduction checks only. The commitment-savings display is an illustration conditional on prespecified cells. Temperature selection is restricted to \(\mathcal F_n^{\mathrm{obs}}\)-measurable rules, including rules based on the displayed plug-in frontier; the plug-in frontier is not claimed to estimate the unobserved oracle regret path. The basic simultaneous upper envelope for the oracle path and its exact transfer to these operational selectors are the settled targets to prove; a sharp small-interval modulus and a two-sided quantile-accuracy guarantee are open.
